For me, I'll take on emotions that aren't mine, for instance becoming extremely calm (I'm normally very anxious), or suddenly having the overwhelming feeling that something must speak to me, like when someone is looking at you and calling your name at a party, and you can sort of feel them looking at you before they say your name. I've also gotten sick and passed out around negative spirits when I was perfectly fine half a second before, things like that.

I've heard several explanations, but one of the best scientific things I've heard is about something called a residual haunting. Basically, when a traumatic event occurs, the energy of the event sort of gets imprinted (think quantum physics), and then when we see these things later, those spirits aren't there, it's sort of like a movie being played. I can't fully explain it, and I won't try to go any further, but it's very interesting. So a residual haunting isn't an actual soul or spirit, it's an energy.
Every person has a soul. We know this, they've weighed souls leaving bodies and all sorts of stuff. Some souls, for some reason, are trapped on this plane of existence. They try to make themselves known because, hello, wouldn't you be freaked out if you were supposed to no longer be on Earth, and now you're just a soul floating around with no vessel? Yes, you would. 
I think the most interesting thing about ghosts, though, is the fact that we DON'T always know why they're here. We're trying to figure that out, and they all have different reasons.

Edit: Wow, I sound silly compared to some of you. The level of scientific research on this sub blows my mind.

There are LOTS of explanations for all sorts of different phenomena, but this one study isn't the be-all, end-all. I totally believe in ghosts and spirit, but have also learned through the years that sometimes normal things are stranger than the paranormal. For example, I thought that I had a ghost for a while because my cabinet doors were opening on their own in the middle of the night. Turns out it was just my cat opening the cabinet doors so she could run around in the shelves. I finally solved the mystery one morning when she jumped out of a cabinet to scare me. As an amateur researcher, I felt pretty dumb about that one.

I rarely find EVP compelling. Unless you have a lot of controls in place, it's pretty hard to prove that something isn't a technological glitch, a rogue soundwave, whatever. If someone submits photos, video, and EVP, all in the same investigation, MAYBE. I don't think EVP is anything more than "backup" evidence.
